swe.problem_statement:
`convert` extended but not imported from Base
This package defines `convert` without importing `Base.convert`, is that intended?

https://github.com/JuliaLinearAlgebra/GenericLinearAlgebra.jl/blob/10b5265b75e123f236ee50b03c845c642462c30e/src/householder.jl#L145

When trying to use it, I also get an error
```julia
julia> GenericLinearAlgebra.convert(Matrix, h2.τ[1])
ERROR: DimensionMismatch: 
Stacktrace:
 [1] lmul!(H::GenericLinearAlgebra.Householder{BigFloat, SubArray{BigFloat, 1, Matrix{BigFloat}, Tuple{UnitRange{Int64}, Int64}, true}}, A::Matrix{BigFloat})
   @ GenericLinearAlgebra ~/.julia/packages/GenericLinearAlgebra/w5JSi/src/householder.jl:24
 [2] convert(#unused#::Type{Matrix}, H::GenericLinearAlgebra.Householder{BigFloat, SubArray{BigFloat, 1, Matrix{BigFloat}, Tuple{UnitRange{Int64}, Int64}, true}})
   @ GenericLinearAlgebra ~/.julia/packages/GenericLinearAlgebra/w5JSi/src/householder.jl:145
 [3] top-level scope
   @ REPL[27]:1
```
swe.pr_description:
Also improve error messages and extend Base's convert instead of defining a new one

Fixes #100
swe.interface:
Function: _hessenberg!(A::StridedMatrix{T}) where T
Location: GenericLinearAlgebra._hessenberg!
Inputs: A – a mutable square matrix (StridedMatrix) whose Hessenberg reduction will be performed in‑place.
Outputs: A Hessenberg factorization object (commonly a struct with fields `τ`, `H`, etc.) that stores the elementary Householder reflectors (`τ`) needed to reconstruct the Hessenberg form. The original matrix `A` is overwritten with the Hessenberg matrix.
Description: Reduces a square matrix to upper Hessenberg form using Householder transformations, returning a lightweight object that holds the reflectors for later application. Used when the test calls `HF = GenericLinearAlgebra._hessenberg!(copy(A))`.

Function: Base.convert(::Type{Matrix}, H::Householder{T}) where T
Location: GenericLinearAlgebra (method extension of Base.convert)
Inputs: `Matrix` – the target abstract type indicating a generic dense matrix; `H` – a `Householder{T}` reflector where `T` is the element type.
Outputs: A dense `Matrix{T}` equal to the matrix representation of the Householder reflector (i.e., `I - τ*v*v'`).
Description: Provides a conversion from a `Householder` reflector to a full dense matrix. The test invokes `HM = convert(Matrix, HF.τ[i])` to obtain the explicit reflector matrix for multiplication.

Function: Base.convert(::Type{Matrix{T}}, H::Householder) where T
Location: GenericLinearAlgebra (method extension of Base.convert)
Inputs: `Matrix{T}` – the concrete matrix type to convert into; `H` – a `Householder` whose element type is compatible with `T`.
Outputs: A dense `Matrix{T}` representing the reflector (`I - τ*v*v'`), constructed with the appropriate element type.
Description: Alias overload that forwards to the generic `convert(Matrix, H)` implementation, ensuring type‑stable conversion to a specific element type. Also exercised indirectly by the test when `HM` is used in matrix multiplications.

llm_metadata.reasoning: The issue reports that GenericLinearAlgebra defines its own `convert` without qualifying it with `Base`, causing a DimensionMismatch when users call `convert(Matrix, ...)`. The added test expects `convert(Matrix, ...)` to work and the reflector size to be length(v)+1. The current implementation returns the wrong size and defines `convert` in the wrong namespace, so the test fails. No test‑suite coupling, hidden naming, external dependencies, ambiguous specs, unrelated patch artifacts, or required domain knowledge are present, making the problem clearly specified and solvable.

review.summary: The commit fixes an incorrect `size` implementation for the `Householder` type. The Householder reflector represents an (n+1)×(n+1) matrix but `size` was returning (n, n) where n = length(H.v). This caused dimension mismatches and incorrect behavior when converting to a dense matrix or using the reflector in eigenvalue/SVD computations.
review.evidence: The `size(H::Householder)` was returning `(length(H.v), length(H.v))` but should return `(length(H.v) + 1, length(H.v) + 1)` since the Householder reflector acts on a space one dimension larger than its stored vector. The `lmul!` function already assumed `length(H.v) == m - 1` (i.e., the matrix dimension is one larger than the vector), confirming the off-by-one in `size`. The PR #101 title 'Fix size of Householder' and new test `_hessenberg! and Hessenberg` that converts individual Householder reflectors to matrices and verifies Hessenberg reduction confirm the bug. Multiple trigger tests (eigenvalue, SVD) also validate the fix.

review.validation_risks: The test uses random matrices so there's a small floating-point tolerance risk, but atol=1e-14 for Float64 is reasonable. The `convert` signature change (adding `Base.` prefix and relaxing type parameter) could theoretically affect method dispatch in edge cases.
review.suggested_tests: 1. Test that `size(Householder(...))` returns the correct dimensions. 2. Test that `convert(Matrix, H)` produces an orthogonal matrix of the correct size. 3. Test round-trip: apply Householder via lmul! and verify result matches dense matrix multiplication.
